simple: When someone joins your game, Roblox shows a plain loading screen while things download. You can swap it for your own screen with your game's name, colors, or a spinning logo. This page shows how to build one with a LocalScript in `ReplicatedFirst`, how to remove the default one, and how to animate yours with `TweenService`. A good loading screen makes your game feel polished from the very first second.
analogy: It is like the curtain in a theater. While the stage crew sets up behind it, the audience looks at a nice curtain with the show's name on it instead of a messy stage.
keyPoints: Put a LocalScript in `ReplicatedFirst`. Things in `ReplicatedFirst` reach the player's device before anything else, so your screen shows up first.
You can build the `ScreenGui` in code, or design it ahead of time and keep it in `ReplicatedFirst`.
Parent your screen to the player's `PlayerGui` and set `IgnoreGuiInset = true` so it covers the whole screen, including the top bar area.
Call `ReplicatedFirst:RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen()` so only your screen shows.
Wait until `game:IsLoaded()` is true, or wait for `game.Loaded`, then destroy your screen.
Add a `task.wait()` if you want your screen to stay up for a minimum time, like 5 seconds.
Use `TweenService` to fade in text or spin an image to show that loading is happening.
You can design the screen in `StarterGui` to preview it, then move it to `ReplicatedFirst` when done.
This page is about joining. Teleport loading screens are set up differently, with `SetTeleportGui()`.

terms.ReplicatedFirst: A special container whose contents get copied to the player's device before anything else in the game.
terms.replicate: Copy from the server to a player's device so it exists there too.
terms.ScreenGui: The container that holds 2D things drawn on the screen, like labels and images.
terms.PlayerGui: The folder inside each player that holds the screens they can currently see.
terms.IgnoreGuiInset: When `true`, the screen also covers the strip at the top where Roblox's buttons are, so there is no gap.
terms.UDim2: A size or position for 2D UI. `UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)` means 100% of the width and 100% of the height, plus 0 extra pixels each.
terms.tween: A smooth change from one value to another over time, like fading transparency from `1` (invisible) to `0` (fully visible) in 1 second.
terms.TweenInfo: Settings for a tween: how long it takes, its easing style, and how many times it repeats. A repeat count of `-1` means repeat forever.
terms.Transparency: How see-through something is. `0` is solid and `1` is fully invisible.
terms.game.Loaded: An event that fires once everything in the game has finished loading on the player's device.

example.title: A simple custom loading screen
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedFirst = game:GetService("ReplicatedFirst")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

-- Make a screen that covers everything
local loadingScreen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
loadingScreen.IgnoreGuiInset = true
loadingScreen.Parent = playerGui

local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0) -- full width and height
label.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(0, 20, 40)
label.TextColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
label.Text = "Loading my game..."
label.TextSize = 32
label.Parent = loadingScreen

-- Hide Roblox's default loading screen
ReplicatedFirst:RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen()

task.wait(3) -- show our screen for at least 3 seconds

if not game:IsLoaded() then
	game.Loaded:Wait() -- wait until everything has loaded
end

loadingScreen:Destroy()
explain: The script runs on the player's device very early because it lives in `ReplicatedFirst`.
It makes a `ScreenGui` and a full-screen `TextLabel` with dark blue background and white text.
`RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen()` hides the Roblox one, so only yours is visible.
It waits at least 3 seconds, then waits for the game to finish loading if it has not yet.
Finally, `Destroy()` removes the loading screen and the player sees the game.

watchOut: Putting the LocalScript somewhere other than `ReplicatedFirst`. It will run too late and players will see the default screen first.
Forgetting to destroy the loading screen. Players will be stuck staring at it forever.
Leaving out `IgnoreGuiInset = true`, which leaves a gap at the top of your screen.
Using a regular Script instead of a LocalScript. Loading screens run on the player's device.
